text: Fill in the key molecule or cofactor that is defective or deficient in each disorder.
questions: A child fed only boiled milk presents with bleeding gums and painful limbs; deficiency of *ascorbic acid/vitamin C:This vitamin keeps hydroxylase iron in the reduced ferrous state.* has disabled the collagen hydroxylases.

An X-linked infant with kinky hair and tortuous arteries has a defective copper transporter, so his *lysyl oxidase:This copper-dependent enzyme oxidises lysine and hydroxylysine side chains to form aldehydes.* cannot cross-link collagen.

A girl with her fourth fracture has a substitution of *glycine/Gly:The smallest amino acid, with only a hydrogen atom as its side chain — it alone fits the crowded helix centre.* by cysteine in her type I collagen, kinking every triple helix the abnormal chain joins.

A tall teenager with lens subluxation and aortic root dilatation has defective *fibrillin-1/fibrillin:Microfibrils made of this glycoprotein scaffold elastin; its defect weakens elastic tissue even though elastin itself is normal.*, the microfibril scaffold for elastic tissue.

A boy with haematuria and sensorineural deafness has mutations in *type IV/IV/type 4/4/collagen IV:This collagen type forms a sheet-like network in basement membranes rather than banded fibres.* collagen of the glomerular and cochlear basement membranes.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each disorder traces to a specific molecular defect: ascorbic acid for hydroxylation (scurvy), lysyl oxidase for cross-linking (Menkes), glycine for helix packing (osteogenesis imperfecta), fibrillin-1 for elastic microfibrils (Marfan), and type IV collagen for basement membranes (Alport).
